title: Separation of Powers under Different Constitutions

content.overview: Comparative constitutional systems implement separation of powers differently: the US model emphasises institutional separation; parliamentary systems fuse executive and legislature through responsibility; Indian practice combines parliamentary government with strong judicial review and basic-structure limits.
content.glance: Compare the model engaged (US-style, parliamentary, Indian); identify the functional equivalent of checks; apply the Indian standard on the facts.
content.study: Comparative study clarifies that separation is a family of designs. The US Constitution separates personnel and functions more sharply. Westminster systems emphasise confidence and ministerial responsibility. India adopts parliamentary executive responsibility while entrusting the judiciary with robust constitutional review. Comparative material is persuasive, not controlling. Current-law framing: always return to Indian text and cases. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: US Model
sections.body: Institutional and personnel separation with checks and balances.

sections.heading: Indian Model
sections.body: Parliamentary executive plus strong judicial review and basic structure.

sections.heading: Use of Comparative Law
sections.body: Persuasive aid, not a substitute for Indian constitutional text.

sections.heading: Application
sections.body: Translate comparative insights into Indian doctrinal categories.

examples.title: US contrast
examples.body: A US-style personnel separation argument is persuasive only; Indian doctrine turns on Ram Jawaya Kapur functional separation and basic structure.

examples.title: Parliamentary fusion
examples.body: Ministers drawn from the legislature is the Indian parliamentary design, not a separation defect.

hypotheticals.question: Is comparative constitutional law binding in India?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is persuasive at best.

hypotheticals.question: Must India copy the US model to have separation of powers?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. India has its own constitutional design of separation and checks.

distinctions.title: US separation vs Indian parliamentary system
distinctions.right: Responsible executive drawn from the legislature

misconceptions.trap: Comparative constitutional law is binding in India.
India must copy the US model to have separation of powers.
misconceptions.correction: India has its own constitutional design of separation and checks.

cases.name: Rai Sahib Ram Jawaya Kapur v State of Punjab
cases.facts: Executive action and constitutional distribution of governmental functions.
cases.issue: What model of separation of powers does the Indian Constitution adopt?
cases.ratioDecidendi: India follows functional differentiation rather than absolute rigidity.
cases.relevance: Indian constitutional baseline for comparative study.

cases.name: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
cases.issue: How does Indian constitutional design constrain concentration of institutional power?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Checks and balances and separation of powers form part of the basic structure.

cases.name: Asif Hameed v State of Jammu and Kashmir
cases.facts: Judicial intervention in fields assigned to other organs.
cases.issue: What is the judicial role under functional separation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must respect the constitutional allocation of functions.
